mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding a permanent fix for receding gums?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is not considered a permanent solution. While it can improve the appearance of areas affected by gum recession in suitable cases, the composite resin material may wear, stain, or chip over time. Bonding may last several years depending on the location, the forces on the tooth, and how it is cared for, but periodic maintenance or replacement may be necessary. It is also important to understand that bonding addresses the cosmetic aspect of recession — it does not regenerate or replace the lost gum tissue itself. Your dentist can advise on the expected longevity based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding for gum recession hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: The procedure is generally minimally invasive. In many cases, little or no tooth preparation is required, and anaesthetic may not be necessary. If the bonding is being applied to a sensitive exposed root surface, your dentist may use a local anaesthetic to help keep you comfortable during the appointment. Many patients experience only mild discomfort during and after the procedure, although experiences vary. Any mild sensitivity following treatment typically settles within a few days.

mainEntity.name: Can receding gums grow back naturally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once gum tissue has receded, it does not typically grow back on its own. This is why prevention and early intervention are important. However, if gum disease is the cause, treating the infection can help to halt further recession and stabilise the condition. In some cases, surgical procedures such as gum grafts may help to restore coverage over exposed root surfaces. Your dentist or periodontist can assess whether your gums could benefit from active treatment to address the recession.

mainEntity.name: How much does composite bonding for receding gums cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of composite bonding varies depending on the number of teeth involved, the extent of the recession, and the complexity of the case. During a consultation, your dentist can provide a personalised treatment plan with clear pricing information. It is worth considering that any underlying gum health issues should be addressed first, which may involve additional treatment. Many dental practices offer payment plans to help spread the cost of treatment.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding better than a gum graft for recession?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are different treatments that serve different purposes, and one is not universally better than the other. Composite bonding is a less invasive cosmetic approach that may improve the appearance of recession relatively quickly in suitable cases. A gum graft is a surgical procedure that aims to restore actual gum tissue coverage and protect the tooth root. The most suitable option depends on the severity of recession, the health of the surrounding tissues, and your individual treatment goals. Your dentist can discuss the advantages and limitations of each approach during a consultation.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my gum recession needs treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all gum recession requires active treatment, but it is always worth having it assessed by a dental professional. If you are experiencing sensitivity, noticing changes in your gumline, or have concerns about the appearance of your teeth, a dental examination can help determine whether treatment is needed and which options may be appropriate. Early assessment is particularly important if you suspect gum disease may be involved, as prompt treatment can help prevent further progression.
